Dom · Altstadt · Burtscheid · RWTH

  1. Must see · Aachen

    Aachener Dom (Pfalzkapelle Karls des Großen)

    Karls des Großen Pfalzkapelle (um 793–813) und 1978 als erste deutsche Stätte in die UNESCO-Welterbeliste aufgenommen. Das oktogonale Zentrum, der Karlsschrein und der Barbarossaleuchter machen den Dom zum Herzstück der Kaiserstadt und zur Krönungskirche der römisch-deutschen Könige.

    Look for cathedral

    Klosterplatz 2, 52062 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Deutsche UNESCO-Kommission, Aachentour, Wikipedia (de/en)

  2. Must see · Aachen

    Aachener Rathaus & Krönungssaal

    Gotisches Rathaus des 14. Jahrhunderts auf den Fundamenten der karolingischen Aula Regia. Im Krönungssaal fanden bis 1531 die Krönungsmahle der römisch-deutschen Könige statt; heute Station der Route Charlemagne.

    Look for townhall

    Markt, 52062 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Rathausaachen, Aachentour, Wikipedia (de/en)

  3. Must see · Aachen

    Elisenbrunnen

    Klassizistische Wandelhalle (1827, nach Ideen Schinkels) über den beiden Trinkbrunnen, aus denen 52 °C warmes, schwefelhaltiges Wasser der Kaiserquelle sprudelt — sichtbares Wahrzeichen von Aachens Thermal- und Bädertradition seit der Römerzeit.

    Look for monument

    Friedrich-Wilhelm-Platz, 52062 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Tourismus NRW e.V. (nrw-tourismus.de), Aachentour, Wikipedia (de/en)

  4. Must see · Rhenish & German · Aachen

    Café Leo van den Daele

    Aachens ältestes Kaffeehaus, 1890 von Leo van den Daele, dem „Printenbaron“, gegründet — verwinkelte Stuben, knarrende Treppen und Mobiliar aus der Aachen-Lütticher Barockzeit. Das Traditionslokal für Reisfladen, hausgemachte Printen und belgisches Gebäck.

    Büchel 18, 52062 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Aachentour, Aachen schöne Altstadt, TravelWorldOnline Traveller

  5. Must see · Rhenish & German · Aachen

    Café & Bäckerei Nobis Printen am Münsterplatz

    Die 1858 gegründete Nobis-Bäckerei am Münsterplatz mit direktem Domblick — die meistbesuchte Filiale und eine der besten Adressen für die geschützte Aachener Printe, dazu Reisfladen, Apfelstrudel und Kakao.

    Münsterplatz 3, 52062 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Aachentour, TravelWorldOnline Traveller, Schwarzaufweiss — Reisemagazin

  6. Must see · Aachen

    Domschatzkammer Aachen

    Einer der bedeutendsten Kirchenschätze Europas und selbst Teil des UNESCO-Welterbes — mit dem Lotharkreuz, der Karlsbüste und dem Aachener Domschatz in einem Gebäude nordwestlich des Doms.

    Look for museum

    Klosterplatz 2, 52062 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Deutsche UNESCO-Kommission, Aachentour

  7. Must see · Aachen

    Carolus Thermen Bad Aachen

    Moderne Thermen- und Saunalandschaft im Stadtgarten, die die über 30 unterirdischen Thermalquellen Aachens (heiß, schwefelhaltig) fortführt. 1998–2001 erbaut, 2020–2022 aufwendig saniert.

    Look for spa

    Passstraße 79, 52070 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Aachentour, Tourismus NRW e.V. (nrw-tourismus.de)

  8. Must see · Aachen

    Centre Charlemagne — Neues Stadtmuseum

    Interaktives Stadtmuseum am Katschhof, das Aachens Geschichte von der Römersiedlung über Karl den Großen bis heute erzählt — der Ausgangspunkt der Route Charlemagne.

    Look for museum

    Katschhof 1, 52062 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Centre Charlemagne — Neues Stadtmuseum Aachen, Aachentour

  9. Must see · Aachen

    Suermondt-Ludwig-Museum

    Die bürgerliche Kunstsammlung Aachens in einem Stadtpalais — mittelalterliche Skulptur, altdeutsche und niederländische Malerei, als „Salon der Stadt“ beschrieben.

    Look for museum

    Wilhelmstraße 18, 52070 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Suermondt-Ludwig-Museum, Aachentour

  10. Must see · Aachen

    Ludwig Forum für Internationale Kunst

    Museum für zeitgenössische Kunst in einer ehemaligen Schirmfabrik der 1920er — Pop-Art, Fotorealismus und aktuelle Positionen aus der Sammlung Peter und Irene Ludwig.

    Look for museum

    Jülicher Straße 97-109, 52070 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Ludwig Forum für Internationale Kunst, Aachentour

  11. Must see · Aachen

    Aachener Weihnachtsmarkt

    Einer der bekanntesten Weihnachtsmärkte Deutschlands, der sich rund um Dom und Rathaus legt — mit Printen, Aachener Dampfnudeln und Glühwein vor der Kulisse des Welterbes. Saisonal (Ende November bis Weihnachten).

    Look for market

    Markt & Katschhof, 52062 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Aachentour, Aachener Zeitung

  12. Must see · Aachen

    Pontstraße & Pontviertel (Studentenviertel)

    Die gastronomische und studentische Ausgehmeile Aachens zwischen Markt und Ponttor — dicht an dicht Cafés, Bars, Kneipen und Restaurants aller Küchen, Herz des von RWTH und FH geprägten Pontviertels.

    Look for district

    Pontstraße, 52062 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Aachentour, Aachen schöne Altstadt

  13. Must see · Rhenish & German · Aachen

    Postwagen Zum Ratskeller

    Historisches Fachwerkhaus aus dem 17. Jahrhundert direkt am Markt neben dem Rathaus — das einzige erhaltene Holzbaugebäude der Altstadt. Rheinisch-Aachener Küche mit Sauerbraten und Himmel un Ääd und Terrasse mit Domblick.

    Krämerstraße 2, 52062 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Aachentour, Wikipedia (de/en)

  14. Must see · Rhenish & German · Aachen

    Am Knipp

    Seit 1698 das älteste Gasthaus Aachens, seit Generationen von der Familie Ramrath geführt — antikes Interieur voller „old-world charm“, Biergarten und deftige regionale Küche (Sauerbraten, Schnitzel, Öcher Spezialitäten). Von der Aachener Zeitung als eines der beliebtesten Traditionslokale ausgezeichnet.

    Bergdriesch 3, 52062 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Aachentour, Aachener Zeitung

  15. Must see · Rhenish & German · Aachen

    La Bécasse

    Seit 1981 die erste Adresse der Region: Patron Christof Lang hält im „La Bécasse“ seit rund einem Vierteljahrhundert einen Michelin-Stern (bestätigt 2026). Reduzierte, geradlinig-klassische Küche mit modernen Elementen.

    Hanbrucher Straße 1, 52064 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Aachener Zeitung

  16. Must see · Rhenish & German · Aachen

    Plaisir by Hamid Heidarzadeh

    Kleines, elegantes Fine-Dining-Restaurant an der Schlossstraße, im Guide Michelin geführt und von Falstaff mit 89 Punkten bewertet. Hamid Heidarzadeh kocht fein gesponnene, fantasievolle Crossover-Menüs, auch vegetarisch.

    Schlossstraße 16, 52066 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Falstaff

    Couven-Museum

    Wohnkultur des Aachener Großbürgertums vom Rokoko über Empire bis Biedermeier, benannt nach den Baumeistern Johann Joseph und Jakob Couven — inklusive der „Adler-Apotheke“ mit der ersten Schokoladenwerbung.

    Look for museum

    Hühnermarkt 17, 52062 Aachen, Germany

    Aachener Tierpark Euregiozoo

    Einer der ältesten Tierparks Deutschlands, im Grünzug am Aachener Stadtrand gelegen, mit rund 500 Tieren aus der Euregio und aller Welt — ein Familienziel.

  19. Worth the detour · Aachen

    Katschhof

    Der zentrale Platz zwischen Dom und Rathaus, einst Innenhof der karolingischen Pfalz. Schauplatz der großen Aachener Veranstaltungen — im Sommer mit „Archimedischem Sandkasten“, im Winter mit dem Weihnachtsmarkt und dem schönsten Domblick.

    Einer der schönsten Plätze der Altstadt, überragt vom Rathaus. In der Mitte steht seit 1334 der Karlsbrunnen, dessen bronzene Karlsfigur (16. Jh.) den Stadtgründer zeigt.

  31. Worth the detour · Aachen

    Puppenbrunnen

    Der beliebte Brunnen von Bonifatius Stirnberg (1975) mit beweglichen Bronzefiguren — Ritter, Narr, Professor, Marktfrau, Pferd — die Facetten der Aachener Stadtgeschichte verkörpern und die man drehen darf.

  32. Worth the detour · Aachen

    Öcher Bend (Volksfest)

    Aachens großes Volksfest, das zweimal im Jahr (Frühjahr und Sommer) auf dem 40.000 m² großen Bendplatz stattfindet — Fahrgeschäfte, Buden und ein modernes Kirmesfest mit langer Tradition.

    Eine der ältesten gastronomischen Perlen der Altstadt direkt am Markt gegenüber dem Rathaus, mit Wurzeln bis ins 14. Jahrhundert. Nach hunderten Jahren Wirtshausgeschichte gab Gastronom Dieter Becker den Schlüssel ab — das Traditionslokal ist inzwischen geschlossen.

    Markt 33, 52062 Aachen, Germany

    Recommended by Aachener Zeitung, t-online Region Aachen (aachen.t-online.de)

StädteRegion Aachen 34

Monschau · Stolberg · Kornelimünster

  1. Must see · StädteRegion Aachen

    Rotes Haus (Scheibler-Museum)

    The Red House was built around 1760 as home and counting-house of cloth merchant Johann Heinrich Scheibler; today it is a museum of 18th–19th-century bourgeois living, famous for its carved free-standing oak staircase and original furnishings.

    Look for historic house museum

    Laufenstraße 10, 52156 Monschau, Germany

    Recommended by StädteRegion Aachen (Freizeit-/Tourenportal), Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info / eifel.de), museen.de

  2. Must see · StädteRegion Aachen

    Burg Monschau

    A well-preserved 13th-century hilltop castle above the Altstadt with a commanding view over the slate roofs of Monschau; today an event venue and youth hostel, and the stage of the summer Monschau Klassik open-air concerts.

    Look for castle

    Auf dem Schloß 4, 52156 Monschau, Germany

    Recommended by Burgen.de, NRW-Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.), Wikipedia (de/en)

  3. Must see · StädteRegion Aachen

    Historischer Ortskern Kornelimünster

    One of Germany's most complete pre-industrial townscapes: 17th–18th-century slate-timber and quarry-stone houses ring the Korneliusmarkt and Benediktusplatz around the former abbey church. The abbey village grew from the 'Monasterium ad Indam' founded in 814 by Benedict of Aniane.

    Look for old town

    Benediktusplatz / Korneliusmarkt, 52076 Aachen-Kornelimünster, Germany

    Recommended by Baukunst NRW (Architektenkammer NRW), Eifelsteig, Stadt Aachen

  4. Must see · StädteRegion Aachen

    Burg Stolberg

    The stone landmark of the Kupferstadt, rising on a limestone crag above the old town and the Vichtbach. The medieval-to-Renaissance castle now hosts events and a Burggastronomie, with wide views over Stolberg's copper-town roofscape.

    Look for castle

    Burgstraße, 52222 Stolberg (Rheinland), Germany

    Recommended by NRW-Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.), Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info / eifel.de), Wikipedia (de/en)

  5. Must see · StädteRegion Aachen

    ENERGETICON

    An energy-and-mining experience museum opened in 2014 on the grounds of the former Grube Anna II colliery — from coal and the Aachen mining district to the future of energy, with preserved pit buildings and hands-on exhibits.

    Look for energy & mining museum

    Konrad-Adenauer-Allee 7, 52477 Alsdorf, Germany

    Recommended by Wikipedia (de/en), NRW-Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.), museen.de

  6. Must see · StädteRegion Aachen

    Dreilägerbachtalsperre

    A drinking-water reservoir of 1909–1911 behind a 38 m-high, 240 m-long dam wall between Roetgen and Rott, in the northern Eifel. A scenic lakeside walk and a section of the Eifelsteig through the Struffelt make it the classic Eifel-gateway outing from Roetgen.

    Look for reservoir / dam

    Dreilägerbachtalsperre, 52159 Roetgen, Germany

    Recommended by Eifelsteig, StädteRegion Aachen (Freizeit-/Tourenportal), Rureifel-Tourismus e.V.

  7. Must see · Rhenish & German · StädteRegion Aachen

    Restaurant Sankt Benedikt

    The area's Michelin-starred anchor since 1979, family-run in a listed dark-red house on the Benediktusplatz; Maximilian Kreus cooks a precise, classically-rooted menu whose signature dish is sturgeon (Stör). Rebuilt after the 2021 flood and starred again.

    Benediktusplatz 12, 52076 Aachen-Kornelimünster, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Gusto (Gusto-online), Der Feinschmecker

  8. Must see · Rhenish & German · StädteRegion Aachen

    Café Kaulard

    A traditional café on Monschau's historic market square, run in the second generation since 1958, known for the local Monschauer Dütchen (thin cream-filled sponge horns) and Printen alongside cakes and coffee.

    Markt 8, 52156 Monschau, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info / eifel.de), Falstaff, Der Feinschmecker

  9. Must see · Rhenish & German · StädteRegion Aachen

    Alte Feuerwache – Podobnik's Restaurant

    In a 1923 former fire station, Kurt Podobnik has cooked refined French menus for half a century — a former Michelin-starred kitchen still rated by Feinschmecker and Gusto, sitting between elevated bistro and gourmet.

    Oppener Straße 115, 52146 Würselen, Germany

    Recommended by Falstaff, Gusto (Gusto-online), Der Feinschmecker

  10. Must see · Rhenish & German · StädteRegion Aachen

    Caffee-Rösterei Wilhelm Maassen

    A coffee roastery run in the fifth family generation in a 300-year-old Monschau townhouse, founded 1862 — beans are still gently drum-roasted for about 15 minutes to old recipes. Der Feinschmecker ranks it among Germany's best roasters; the house also makes a 'Caffeebier' (a full beer refined with Brazilian espresso).

    Stadtstraße 24, 52156 Monschau, Germany

    Recommended by Der Feinschmecker, Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info / eifel.de), Aachener Zeitung

  11. Must see · StädteRegion Aachen

    Historische Altstadt Monschau

    Around 300 listed slate-and-timber Fachwerk houses crowd the narrow lanes of the Rur valley, the best-preserved cloth-makers' town in the Eifel and the postcard image of Monschau. Its Blütezeit came from 18th-century wool-cloth (Monschauer Tuch), prized across Europe.

    Look for old town

    Altstadt / Am Markt, 52156 Monschau, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info / eifel.de), AG Historische Stadt- und Ortskerne in NRW

  12. Must see · StädteRegion Aachen

    Burg Rode

    First documented in 1104 as 'castrum Rodense', Herzogenrath's best-known landmark stands above the Wurm with a 14th-century tower reshaped in the 19th century. Now a cultural venue with exhibitions on the castle's history and the 18th-century Bockreiter robber band.

    Look for castle

    Burg Rode, 52134 Herzogenrath, Germany

    Recommended by KuLaDig — Kultur.Landschaft.Digital (LVR), Stadt Herzogenrath

  13. Must see · Rhenish & German · StädteRegion Aachen

    Schnabuleum (Historische Senfmühle)

    The restaurant of the historic Monschau mustard mill, where every dish is refined with the house's own hand-milled Moutarde de Montjoie — a Senfbraten (mustard pot roast) and mustard-sauce plates are the signature. In the restored listed mill building.

    Laufenstraße 118, 52156 Monschau, Germany

    Recommended by Falstaff, NRW-Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.)

  14. Worth the detour · StädteRegion Aachen

    Kunsthaus NRW / ehem. Reichsabtei Kornelimünster

    The former Imperial Abbey, rebuilt in 1721 as a late-baroque palace, houses the Kunsthaus NRW — the state of North Rhine-Westphalia's art collection of over 5,000 works from Rhenish Expressionism to the present, shown in the abbey's grand halls and garden.

    Look for art museum

    Abteigarten 6, 52076 Aachen-Kornelimünster, Germany

    Recommended by Kunsthaus NRW Kornelimünster, Wikipedia (de/en), museen.de

  15. Worth the detour · StädteRegion Aachen

    Propsteikirche St. Kornelius

    The former abbey church and today's parish church, a landmark of Rhenish architecture whose 814–817 founding core hides beneath a seemingly Gothic five-aisled body — over 1,000 years of building history. A pilgrimage site for its Corneliusreliquien (Cornelius relics).

    Look for pilgrimage church

    Korneliusmarkt, 52076 Aachen-Kornelimünster, Germany

    Recommended by Baukunst NRW (Architektenkammer NRW), Eifelführer, KuLaDig — Kultur.Landschaft.Digital (LVR)

  16. Worth the detour · StädteRegion Aachen

    Historischer Altstadtkern Stolberg

    Narrow stepped lanes and small squares of half-timbered and local-limestone houses with hewn bluestone (Blaustein) trim, climbing beneath Burg Stolberg — a townscape shaped by the 17th–18th-century copper and brass boom.

    Look for old town

    Altstadt / Burgstraße, 52222 Stolberg (Rheinland), Germany

    Recommended by Rureifel-Tourismus e.V., StädteRegion Aachen (Freizeit-/Tourenportal), AG Historische Stadt- und Ortskerne in NRW

  17. Worth the detour · StädteRegion Aachen

    Kupferhof Rosenthal

    A baroque copper-master's courtyard house built in 1724 by Tillmann Roland, monument-protected since 1986 — one of the finest of Stolberg's Kupferhöfe, the fortified merchant-workshop yards found nowhere else in Germany.

    Look for copper courtyard house

    Rathausstraße 67, 52222 Stolberg (Rheinland), Germany

    Recommended by Eifelsteig, Rureifel-Tourismus e.V., Wikipedia (de/en)

  18. Worth the detour · StädteRegion Aachen

    Museum Zinkhütter Hof

    A museum of the Aachen region's industrial, economic and social history in a former 19th-century glassworks — 'Stolberger Zink', 'Aachener Nadel' (needle-making) and brass, one of the best-preserved examples of the historic industrial belt from Aachen through Stolberg to Eschweiler.

    Look for industrial museum

    Cockerillstraße 90, 52222 Stolberg (Rheinland), Germany

    Recommended by museen.de, Wikipedia (de/en), Rureifel-Tourismus e.V.

  19. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · StädteRegion Aachen

    Venngasthof Zur Buche

    A family-run country inn on the Eifelsteig at the Hohes Venn above Monschau, called one of the best addresses in the Nordeifel. The kitchen runs home-style and Mediterranean plates with constantly changing daily specials — the Argentine rumpsteaks, the Buche-Burger and schnitzel are the crowd-pleasers.

    Im Brand 39, 52156 Monschau (Mützenich), Germany

    Recommended by Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info / eifel.de), Rureifel-Tourismus e.V., Eifelsteig

  20. Worth the detour · StädteRegion Aachen

    Historische Senfmühle Monschau

    A working mustard mill grinding by hand since 1882, now in the 4th–5th generation, producing the celebrated Moutarde de Montjoie (Monschauer Senf) in over twenty varieties. Mill tours, a shop and the adjoining Schnabuleum restaurant occupy the restored listed building.

    Look for mustard mill

    Laufenstraße 118, 52156 Monschau, Germany

    Recommended by NRW-Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.), DuMont Reise

  21. Worth the detour · StädteRegion Aachen

    Wurmtal (Naturschutzgebiet)

    A green regional recreation corridor along the Wurm river between Aachen and Herzogenrath — meadow, wetland and forest with small lakes and the old mine dumps (Halden) of the Aachen coal district, laced with cycle and hiking paths.

    Look for nature reserve / river valley

    Wurmtal, 52134 Herzogenrath, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Herzogenrath, KuLaDig — Kultur.Landschaft.Digital (LVR)

  22. Worth the detour · StädteRegion Aachen

    Burg Wilhelmstein

    A castle ruin on the eastern bank of the Wurm near Würselen-Bardenberg, set directly in the Wurmtal; for over twenty summers its open-air stage has hosted the city's popular Freiluft programme of concerts, cabaret and film.

    Look for castle ruin

    Burg Wilhelmstein, 52146 Würselen-Bardenberg, Germany

    Recommended by StädteRegion Aachen (Freizeit-/Tourenportal), Lebendiges Aachen

  23. Worth the detour · StädteRegion Aachen

    Carl-Alexander-Park (Grube Carl-Alexander)

    The ~80 m mining spoil heap of the former Grube Carl-Alexander colliery, greened and opened for EuRegionale 2008 — a suspension bridge climbs to a viewpoint high above the treetops with a panorama over Baesweiler and the surrounding towns.

    Look for mining heap park / viewpoint

    Carl-Alexander-Park, 52499 Baesweiler, Germany

    Recommended by Wikipedia (de/en), KuLaDig — Kultur.Landschaft.Digital (LVR)

  24. Worth the detour · StädteRegion Aachen

    Naturschutzgebiet Struffelt

    A heath-and-moor nature reserve on the Eifelsteig above Roetgen — 'the gateway to the Eifel' — with a circular premium trail (Roetgener Schleife) linking the ridge to the Dreilägerbachtalsperre.

    Look for heath nature reserve

    Struffelt, 52159 Roetgen, Germany

    Recommended by Gemeinde Roetgen, Eifelsteig

  25. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · StädteRegion Aachen

    Konditorei-Café am Roten Haus

    A patisserie-café in a listed former cloth-merchant's house opposite the Rotes Haus, making Monschau's own specialties — Vennbrocken and Dütchen, truffles and cakes — to family recipes, with a sunny terrace over the Rur.

    Laufenstraße 11, 52156 Monschau, Germany

    Recommended by Erlebnis-Region (Euregio Maas-Rhein), Isg Monschau (Interessengemeinschaft Stadtbild)

  26. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · StädteRegion Aachen

    Restaurant Gut Schwarzenbruch

    German and Mediterranean cooking served in a historic country estate with an ornate dining hall on Stolberg's edge — a long-standing regional address for a special-occasion meal.

    Gut Schwarzenbruch 2, 52222 Stolberg (Rheinland), Germany

    Recommended by Schlemmer Atlas, Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info / eifel.de)

  27. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · StädteRegion Aachen

    Landgasthof Gut Marienbildchen

    A country inn in an early-19th-century manor on the edge of Roetgen, surrounded by meadows on the Eifelsteig — regional Eifel cooking with game (Wild) in season, a classic stop at the gateway to the Eifel.

    Münsterbildchen 3, 52159 Roetgen, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info / eifel.de), Eifelsteig

  28. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · StädteRegion Aachen

    Hotel-Restaurant-Café Horchem

    A hotel-restaurant-café in the heart of Monschau run by chef Lutz Schell, cooking regional and seasonal Eifel plates plus Belgian beers and its own cakes. Its sunny 'Venedig-Blick' terrace looks across the Rur to the Rotes Haus and the evangelical church, and a modern Braukeller lounge bar was added in 2014.

    Rurstraße 14, 52156 Monschau, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info / eifel.de), de-eifel.de

  29. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · StädteRegion Aachen

    Restaurant Mirabela

    In the heart of the Eifel-gateway town of Roetgen, the Kosor family run one of the most popular local addresses for light, freshly-prepared Mediterranean cooking — meat, fish, soups and salads — with a garden terrace and Croatian wines. Regional artists' paintings hang in the bright dining rooms.

    Hauptstraße 49, 52159 Roetgen, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info / eifel.de), Roetgen-Touristik

  30. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · StädteRegion Aachen

    Restaurant Eduard

    A restaurant on the grounds of the Energeticon — the former Grube-Anna colliery — in Alsdorf, serving modern crossover cooking and a changing recommendation card built on seasonal regional produce in a striking industrial-heritage setting. Reopened after an insolvency under a new operator and kitchen.

    Konrad-Adenauer-Allee 7, 52477 Alsdorf, Germany

    Recommended by Aachener Zeitung, Top Magazin Aachen (top-aachen.de)

  31. Deep cut · StädteRegion Aachen

    Kupferhof Grünenthal

    A historic Stolberg copper yard and the founding seat of the Grünenthal pharmaceutical company, still held by the Wirtz family — another of the town's more-than-ten Kupferhöfe that trace its industrial golden age.

    Look for copper courtyard house

    Steinfeldstraße, 52222 Stolberg (Rheinland), Germany

    Recommended by StädteRegion Aachen (Freizeit-/Tourenportal), Wikipedia (de/en), KuLaDig — Kultur.Landschaft.Digital (LVR)

  32. Deep cut · StädteRegion Aachen

    Monschauer Glashütte

    A glassblowing workshop below the castle where you can watch a Glasbläser at work — a nod to the town's second historic craft alongside cloth-making — with a shop and demonstrations.

    Look for glassworks

    Burgau 15, 52156 Monschau, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info / eifel.de), Eifelsteig

  33. Deep cut · Rhenish & German · StädteRegion Aachen

    Café-Bistro Grünental

    A lovingly-run café-bistro set alone in the woods on the Roetgen–Monschau border by the Eifelsteig, cooking regional and seasonal dishes and cakes. Open seasonally (roughly April to October, Fri–Sun) and a beloved rest stop for hikers.

    Grünental 1, 52156 Monschau, Germany

    Recommended by NRW-Tourismus (Tourismus NRW e.V.), Eifel-Tour (eifel-tour.de)

  34. Closed — kept for the record · StädteRegion Aachen

    Felsenkeller Brauhaus & Museum — CLOSED

    Founded in 1847, the Felsenkeller was a four-generation Monschau brewery (Felsquell Pils, naturally cloudy Zwickelbier) that later became the Eifel's first brewery museum. The brewery museum closed in 2019; it remains a landmark of the region's brewing heritage.

    Look for brewery museum

    Laufenstraße, 52156 Monschau, Germany

    Recommended by BRF (Belgischer Rundfunk), Industriemuseen Euregio Maas-Rhein

Eifel & Düren, DE 38

National Park · Nideggen · Jülich

  1. Must see · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Zitadelle Jülich & Museum Zitadelle

    A 90,000 m² fortress and ducal palace — the most significant Italian High-Renaissance citadel north of the Alps and one of the best-preserved early-modern fortresses in Europe. Ramparts, casemates and the restored palace chapel can be toured, and the Museum Zitadelle traces Jülich from Roman times through the Renaissance to Prussia.

    Look for Renaissance citadel & museum

    Schlossstraße 6, 52428 Jülich, Germany

    Recommended by Museum Zitadelle Jülich, Kreis Düren Tourismus, Stadt Jülich, WP

  2. Must see · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Vogelsang IP

    A former Nazi 'Ordensburg' above the Urftsee, one of the largest surviving complexes of Nazi architecture, reborn as an international visitor centre. It houses the Nationalpark-Zentrum Eifel and a 48 m observation tower reached by a historic spiral staircase, with panoramic views over the Dreiborn plateau.

    Look for Visitor centre / former Ordensburg

    Vogelsang 70, 53937 Schleiden, Germany

    Recommended by Nationalpark Eifel, Tourismus NRW e.V. (nrw-tourismus.de), Eifel.de (Eifel Tourismus)

  3. Must see · Eifel & Düren, DE

    NS-Dokumentation Vogelsang — 'Bestimmung: Herrenmensch'

    The permanent exhibition (opened 2016) confronting the history of the NS-Ordensburgen 'between fascination and crime' across 800 m². As a recognised memorial site it documents how the NSDAP trained its leadership cadre here between 1936 and 1939.

    Look for Documentation centre / memorial

    Vogelsang 70, 53937 Schleiden, Germany

    Recommended by Gedenkstätten NRW, Memorial Museums, WP

  4. Must see · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Burg Nideggen & Burgenmuseum

    Built 1177–1191 by the Counts of Jülich and long reputed impregnable, this red-sandstone castle sits high above the Rur valley, protected on three sides by sheer cliffs. Its keep has housed the Burgenmuseum since 1979, showing how people lived and worked in the medieval Rhineland and Eifel.

    Look for Castle & museum

    Burg Nideggen, Kirchgasse, 52385 Nideggen, Germany

    Recommended by Rureifel-Tourismus e.V., Kreis Düren Tourismus, WP

  5. Must see · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Buntsandsteinfelsen & Buntsandsteinroute Nideggen

    The Rur valley around Nideggen is walled by steeply towering red-sandstone (Buntsandstein) cliffs — a protected landscape and one of the Eifel's signature geological sights. The waymarked Buntsandsteinroute threads the crags and rewards with dramatic valley views; the same red stone built the town's gates and walls.

    Look for Red-rock cliffs / hiking route

    Buntsandsteinfelsen im Rurtal, 52385 Nideggen, Germany

    Recommended by Rureifel-Tourismus e.V., Eifelsteig, Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info)

  6. Must see · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Jugendstil-Wasserkraftwerk Heimbach

    When it opened in 1905 at the foot of the Urft dam it was the largest hydroelectric power station in the world; today it is celebrated as Germany's most beautiful power station, a working Art Nouveau (Jugendstil) hall. Free guided tours run daily and let you see the machine hall's original grandeur.

    Look for Art Nouveau hydro power station

    Wasserkraftwerk, 52396 Heimbach, Germany

    Recommended by Rureifel-Tourismus e.V., Kreis Düren Tourismus, Eifelsteig

  7. Must see · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Rurtalsperre Schwammenauel & Rursee

    The Rur was dammed at Schwammenauel in the 1930s to create the 8 km² Rursee — the 'Amazon of the Eifel' — one of Germany's largest reservoirs at 205 million m³. Its 480 m dam wall and the surrounding hiking and cycling shoreline make it the recreational heart of the Rureifel.

    Look for Reservoir / dam

    Rurtalsperre Schwammenauel, 52396 Heimbach, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel.de (Eifel Tourismus), Rureifel-Tourismus e.V., Rursee-Touristik GmbH

  8. Must see · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Leopold-Hoesch-Museum Düren

    Founded 1905 and expanded in 2010 with a Peter Kulka extension, Düren's fine-art museum holds an outstanding collection of classical modernism, Expressionism, concrete art and the ZERO movement. One of the Rhineland's serious art addresses, in a striking Jugendstil-plus-modern building.

    Look for Art museum

    Hoeschplatz 1, 52349 Düren, Germany

    Recommended by Leopold-Hoesch-Museum & Papiermuseum Düren, Tourismus NRW e.V. (nrw-tourismus.de), WP

  9. Must see · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Heimbacher Brauhaus

    Heimbach's own brewhouse pours three house beers — a mild light, a hearty dark and a low-carbonation Zwickel/Kellerbier — alongside Eifel-typical plates. After Kölsch in Cologne and Alt in Düsseldorf, it gave the Rureifel its own 'Heimbacher Bier'.

    Schwammenauel 6, 52396 Heimbach, Germany

    Recommended by Rureifel-Tourismus e.V., Eifelsteig, Kreis Düren Tourismus

  10. Must see · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Nationalpark Eifel

    NRW's only national park, protecting beech forests, wild daffodil meadows and the Rur/Urft lake country between Monschau and Düren; a certified Dark-Sky park where 'wilderness is allowed to happen'. Free-access trails, ranger tours and four Nationalpark-Tore make it the anchor of the whole Rureifel.

    Look for National park

    Nationalpark Eifel, 53937 Schleiden-Gemünd, Germany

    Recommended by Nationalpark Eifel, Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info)

  11. Must see · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Wilder Kermeter & Wilder Weg

    A barrier-free wilderness area on the Kermeter ridge with a 6.2 km trail network and the interactive ten-station Wilder Weg nature-education path. Short spurs reach the Hirschley viewpoint, where the forest opens onto a sweeping view over the Rursee.

    Look for Nature trail / viewpoint

    Kermeter, 52396 Heimbach, Germany

    Recommended by Nationalpark Eifel, Nordeifel Tourismus

  12. Must see · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Wettsteins Restaurant

    A MICHELIN-Guide country restaurant a little off the beaten track in Langerwehe, on the Düren edge of the Eifel, cooking regionally-influenced food to choose as a set menu or à la carte — grilled meats such as rumpsteak alongside classics like schnitzel and roast joint, with a summer terrace.

    Schlossstraße 66, 52379 Langerwehe, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland

  13. Worth the detour · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Wüstung Wollseifen

    A ghost village on the Dreiborn plateau: its ~550 residents were expelled in 1946 so the site could become a troop training ground, used by Belgian forces until 2005. Since the national park opened in 2006 the ruins are freely accessible — the St-Rochus church, the old school and a wayside chapel still stand.

    Look for Abandoned village / historic site

    Wollseifen, Dreiborner Hochfläche, 53937 Schleiden, Germany

    Recommended by KuLaDig — Kultur.Landschaft.Digital (LVR), WP, Nationalpark Eifel

  14. Worth the detour · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Abtei Mariawald

    Perched at 417 m above Heimbach in the heart of the national park, Mariawald was Germany's last Trappist monastery until the community dissolved in 2018. The site is being rebuilt as a spiritual centre and remains open to visitors, with near-daily guided tours of the cloister, a shop, guesthouse and its own liqueur and Trappist beer.

    Look for Former Trappist abbey / pilgrimage site

    Mariawald, 52396 Heimbach, Germany

    Recommended by Rureifel-Tourismus e.V., katholisch.de, Stadt Heimbach

  15. Worth the detour · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Burg Hengebach

    Heimbach's landmark castle, dating to the 11th century, stands 200 m up on its greywacke rock over the old town. Courtyard, wall-walk and keep are open free year-round, and the castle now houses the Internationale Kunstakademie Heimbach.

    Look for Medieval castle / art academy

    Burg Hengebach, 52396 Heimbach, Germany

    Recommended by Stadt Heimbach, Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info), Rureifel-Tourismus e.V.

  16. Worth the detour · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Heimbach — Altstadt & NRW's smallest town

    The smallest town in North Rhine-Westphalia, tucked in the Rur valley below the Rursee and the Kermeter, with half-timbered houses, galleries, taverns and street cafés under Burg Hengebach. A compact base uniting the Jugendstil power station, the art academy and the national-park gate in one riverside stroll.

    Look for Historic small town

    Altstadt, 52396 Heimbach, Germany

    Recommended by Rureifel-Tourismus e.V., Eifelsteig, Stadt Heimbach

  17. Worth the detour · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Rursee-Schifffahrt

    Passenger boats run four scenic circuits of two to four hours across the Rursee and Obersee, calling at landing stages from Schwammenauel and Woffelsbach to Rurberg, the Urft dam and Einruhr. The classic car-free way to reach trailheads deep inside the national park.

    Look for Lake cruises

    Rursee-Schifffahrt, Seeufer, 52152 Simmerath-Rurberg, Germany

    Recommended by Rureifel-Tourismus e.V., Eifelsteig, Rursee-Touristik GmbH

  18. Worth the detour · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Urftsee & Urftstaumauer

    The Urft was dammed in 1905 — one of Germany's oldest large dams — to form the Urftsee, which together with the Rursee and Obersee makes up the Eifeler Seenplatte. The historic curved masonry Urftstaumauer sits below Vogelsang, ringed by national-park forest and reachable on foot or by boat.

    Look for Reservoir / historic dam

    Urftstaumauer, 53937 Schleiden, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel.de (Eifel Tourismus), Rursee-Touristik GmbH, Nationalpark Eifel

  19. Worth the detour · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Nationalpark-Tor Rurberg

    One of the national park's gateway centres, with the free permanent exhibition 'Lebensadern der Natur' on the region's rivers, lakes and ponds — river crayfish, pearl mussels and beavers among them — plus tourist information and a digital terrain model. A prime starting point for free ranger tours.

    Look for National-park gateway / exhibition

    Seeufer 3, 52152 Simmerath-Rurberg, Germany

    Recommended by Nationalpark Eifel, Eifel.de (Eifel Tourismus), Rursee-Touristik GmbH

  20. Worth the detour · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Papiermuseum Düren

    Next door to the Leopold-Hoesch-Museum, the award-winning Paper Museum (2018, by architect Klaus Hollenbeck) tells the story of paper — its making, use and Düren's own paper-industry heritage — with folding, watermarking and embossing built into the architecture itself.

    Look for Paper museum

    Hoeschplatz, 52349 Düren, Germany

    Recommended by Leopold-Hoesch-Museum & Papiermuseum Düren, Tourismus NRW e.V. (nrw-tourismus.de), arthistoricum.net

  21. Worth the detour · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Annakirche (St. Anna) Düren

    Düren's medieval pilgrimage church to the relic of St Anna — once called 'the cathedral of Düren' — was flattened in the 1944 bombing and rebuilt by Rudolf and Maria Schwarz (1951–56) as a landmark of modern sacred architecture, using rubble stone from across the ruined city to let the old church symbolically rise again.

    Look for Modernist pilgrimage church

    Annakirchplatz, 52349 Düren, Germany

    Recommended by baukunst-nrw, Straße der Moderne, KuLaDig — Kultur.Landschaft.Digital (LVR)

  22. Worth the detour · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Brückenkopf-Park Jülich

    A star-shaped Napoleonic bridgehead fortress on the left bank of the Rur, raised in the early 19th century to guard the river crossing and converted to a public park in 1929. Its 33 ha now hold gardens, woodland and a family zoo around the preserved fortifications — one of the few Jülich structures to survive the 1944 devastation.

    Look for Napoleonic fortress park

    Rurauenstraße 11, 52428 Jülich, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel.de (Eifel Tourismus), KuLaDig — Kultur.Landschaft.Digital (LVR), Kreis Düren Tourismus

  23. Worth the detour · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Perlenbach-Fuhrtsbachtal — Narzissenblüte (Hohes Venn edge)

    On the German edge of the Hohes Venn, this 331 ha reserve turns golden each spring as over 10 million wild daffodils bloom in the narrow Perlenbach and Fuhrtsbach valleys — a phenomenon unique in Europe. The Narzissenroute from Monschau-Höfen, an Eifelsteig partner trail, is the classic way to see it.

    Look for Nature reserve / daffodil valley

    Perlenbach-Fuhrtsbachtal, 52156 Monschau-Höfen, Germany

    Recommended by Eifelsteig, Aachener Zeitung, Eifel.de (Eifel Tourismus)

  24. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Burgrestaurant Nideggen

    The restaurant inside 12th-century Burg Nideggen, cultivating the Eifel's culinary heritage with seasonal, mostly regional market cooking. Here chefs Herbert Brockel and Tobias Schlimbach held a Michelin star (as 'Brockel Schlimbach', 2019–2025); the venue now continues as a regional restaurant and event location on the castle rock.

    Kirchgasse 10a, 52385 Nideggen, Germany

    Recommended by Der Feinschmecker, Aachener Zeitung, Guide Michelin Deutschland

  25. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Gastro Vogelsang — Panorama-Restaurant

    The excursion restaurant inside the Vogelsang IP forum, with a light-filled dining room and terrace giving a panoramic view over the Urftsee and the Dreiborn plateau. Changing daily dishes built around the best natural products of the Eifel, plus coffee and cake.

    Vogelsang 71, 53937 Schleiden, Germany

    Recommended by Nationalpark Eifel, Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info), Eifelsteig

  26. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Hotel-Restaurant Zum kleinen Seehof

    A waterfront restaurant in Woffelsbach directly on the Rursee, its charm coming from the lakeside setting. The kitchen serves Eifel specialities, fish and seasonal dishes, plus coffee and cake with a view of the water.

    Woffelsbach, 52152 Simmerath, Germany

    Recommended by Nationalpark Eifel, Eifelsteig, Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info)

  27. Worth the detour · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Wildnis-Trail Nationalpark Eifel

    The national park's signature long-distance path — about 85 km in four stages from Monschau-Höfen across the Kermeter to Zerkall/Nideggen — leading through the park's wildest core of beech forest, moor and lake. The through-hike that strings together most of the Eifel's landscape sights.

    Look for Long-distance wilderness trail

    Wildnis-Trail (Höfen–Zerkall), 53937 Schleiden, Germany

    Recommended by Nationalpark Eifel, Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info)

  28. Worth the detour · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Dreiborner Hochfläche

    The open plateau below Vogelsang — a former Belgian troop training ground now returning to grassland, heath and returning wildlife inside the national park. Wide skies, red deer and free walking and cycling routes past Wollseifen make it one of the park's most distinctive open landscapes.

    Look for Plateau landscape / viewpoint

    Dreiborner Hochfläche, 53937 Schleiden, Germany

    Recommended by Nationalpark Eifel, Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info)

  29. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Eifeler Hof am Rursee

    A cosy restaurant-café in the heart of Heimbach, run since 1919, with continuous warm and cold service focused on regional Eifel specialities and a beer garden and covered terrace toward the Rursee.

    Hengebachstraße 43-45, 52396 Heimbach, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info), Rureifel-Tourismus e.V.

  30. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Eifelhaus Einruhr

    Right on the Obersee shore by the boat dock, a Nationalpark-Gastgeber serving a broad menu made from regional Eifel products, plus homemade cake and ice cream and coffee from its own roastery, on a large lakeside terrace.

    Am Obersee 1, 52152 Simmerath-Einruhr, Germany

    Recommended by Nationalpark Eifel, Rureifel-Tourismus e.V.

  31. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Hotel-Restaurant Kermeterschänke

    A rustic wild-game inn at 525 m in Wolfgarten, the only settlement wholly surrounded by the national park, with the Wildnis-Trail passing the door. Long famous regionally for game from the surrounding forests and fresh trout, plus homemade cakes.

    Kermeterstraße 4, 53937 Schleiden-Wolfgarten, Germany

    Recommended by Nationalpark Eifel, Eifel.de (Eifel Tourismus)

  32. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Hotel-Restaurant Roeb

    A family hotel-restaurant in Nideggen-Schmidt with a constantly changing specialty menu of typical Eifel dishes cooked from fresh regional produce, in a cosy setting on the Kermeter side of the Rur valley.

    Monschauer Straße 1, 52385 Nideggen-Schmidt, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel.de (Eifel Tourismus), Rureifel-Tourismus e.V.

  33. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Gemünder Parkrestaurant

    A long-running German restaurant by the Kurpark in Schleiden-Gemünd, at the western gateway to the national park, known for regional Eifel cooking with game dishes and sauerbraten to the fore.

    Kurhausstraße 5, 53937 Schleiden-Gemünd, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel.de (Eifel Tourismus), Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info)

  34. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Hotel-Restaurant Seemöwe

    A lakeside hotel-restaurant on the banks of the Obersee at Rurberg, offering hot and cold Eifel cooking with game and trout dishes as the specialities.

    Am Obersee 10, 52152 Simmerath-Rurberg, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info), Rureifel-Tourismus e.V.

  35. Worth the detour · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Genießer Wirtshaus

    A MICHELIN-Guide 'good cooking' country inn in the Simmerath district of Hövel, in the Rureifel near the national park, serving hearty regional Landküche. Inspector-selected for honest country cooking at a fair price.

    Hövel 15, 52152 Simmerath, Germany

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland

  36. Deep cut · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Ausstellung 'Rur und Fels' Nideggen-Brück

    The Biologische Station Düren turned the old freight shed of the Nideggen-Brück station into a free natural-history exhibition on the twin habitats of the Rur floodplain and the sandstone cliffs, with beavers, steppe grasshoppers and grass snakes shown in vivid dioramas.

    Look for Nature exhibition

    Bahnhof Nideggen-Brück, 52385 Nideggen-Brück, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel.de (Eifel Tourismus), Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info)

  37. Deep cut · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Klostergastronomie Abtei Mariawald

    The gastronomy of former Trappist Mariawald, carried on after the monks left in 2018: the herbal Mariawalder Klosterlikör (a recipe over a century old) and a revived Nemus Mariae Trappist Tripel brewed to the abbey's original recipe, served at the monastery above Heimbach.

    Mariawald, 52396 Heimbach, Germany

    Recommended by katholisch.de, Stadt Mechernich

  38. Deep cut · Rhenish & German · Eifel & Düren, DE

    Café Burgblick (Konditorei-Café Krupp)

    An excursion café-Konditorei (Café Krupp) above the Rur in Heimbach with a large sun terrace and a wide choice of cakes and baked goods from its own bakery, plus coffee, ice cream and light lunch dishes — a classic Rureifel Kaffee-und-Kuchen stop with a view toward Burg Hengebach.

    Über Rur 3, 52396 Heimbach, Germany

    Recommended by Eifel Tourismus (eifel.info / eifel.de), Schlemmerregion Aachen-Eifel-Euregio

Dutch South Limburg 44

Maastricht · Vaals · Valkenburg

  1. Must see · Dutch & Limburgs · Dutch South Limburg

    Cafe Sjiek

    The address for Maastricht's sweet-sour braised zoervleisj, cooked the old way and served with fries - long the connoisseurs' pick, and awarded a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2025.

    Sint Pieterstraat 13, 6211 JM Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Foodies Magazine, Puur Zuid-Limburg

  2. Must see · Dutch South Limburg

    Sint-Servaasbasiliek

    The Netherlands' oldest church, over the tomb of St Servatius, set between the Vrijthof and Keizer Karelplein. Its Schatkamer (treasury) holds the jewelled Noodkist reliquary and one of Europe's great collections of early-medieval Oriental silks.

    Look for Basilica & treasury

    Keizer Karelplein 3, Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Visit Maastricht, Visit Zuid-Limburg

  3. Must see · Dutch South Limburg

    Onze-Lieve-Vrouwebasiliek

    A powerful Romanesque basilica (the fortress-like Westwerk is its signature) on Maastricht's most atmospheric square. Pilgrims still light candles at the 15th-century 'Sterre der Zee' (Star of the Sea) image of the Virgin.

    Look for Romanesque basilica

    Onze Lieve Vrouweplein 7, Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Wikipedia (de/en), Rijksmonumenten.nl

  4. Must see · Dutch South Limburg

    Boekhandel Dominicanen

    A 13th-century Dominican church, the first Gothic church of the Low Countries, reborn as a bookshop under towering vaults and a monumental steel bookcase. Voted the world's most beautiful bookstore (2025), it draws roughly a million visitors a year.

    Look for Bookshop in a Gothic church

    Dominicanerkerkstraat 1, Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Visit Maastricht, WNL

  5. Must see · Dutch South Limburg

    Bonnefantenmuseum

    Limburg's leading art museum, from old masters to contemporary, in Aldo Rossi's landmark E-shaped building with a rocket-shaped cupola on the Maas. The brick 'Treppestraat' staircase is a destination in itself.

    Look for Art museum

    Avenue Céramique 250, Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Bonnefanten (official), Wikipedia (de/en)

  6. Must see · Dutch South Limburg

    Grotten Noord (Sint-Pietersberg)

    A guided descent ~30 m into the Sint-Pietersberg marl, through part of a labyrinth of once 20,000+ passages carved over centuries by block-cutters, walls covered in charcoal drawings and names. Cool year-round; wartime hiding place.

    Look for Marl cave labyrinth

    Luikerweg 80, 6212 NH Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Explore Maastricht (Maastricht Underground), Natuurmonumenten

  7. Must see · Dutch South Limburg

    Vrijthof

    Maastricht's grand stage - terraces, the basilica and the red-towered Sint-Janskerk framing a square often called the finest in the Netherlands, and home to Andre Rieu's summer concerts and the Vrijthof museum.

    Look for Grand square

    Vrijthof, Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Visit Maastricht, Wikipedia (de/en)

  8. Must see · Dutch South Limburg

    Sint Servaasbrug

    The oldest bridge in the Netherlands - a seven-arch limestone span built around 1280-1298 that has linked the old town to Wyck across the Maas for seven centuries; now a pedestrian icon of the city.

    Look for Medieval stone bridge

    Sint Servaasbrug, Maasboulevard, Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Visit Maastricht, Via Belgica

  9. Must see · Dutch South Limburg

    Drielandenpunt / Vaalserberg

    The highest point of the mainland Netherlands (322.5 m) where the borders of the Netherlands, Germany and Belgium meet. Straddle three countries at once, climb the Wilhelmina and Boudewijn observation towers, and lose the kids in one of Europe's largest hedge mazes.

    Look for Tri-border summit

    Viergrenzenweg, Vaalserberg, Vaals, Netherlands

    Recommended by Wikipedia (de/en), Het Drielandenpunt (official)

  10. Must see · Dutch South Limburg

    Kasteelruine & Fluweelengrot Valkenburg

    The only true hilltop castle in the Netherlands - a beacon over Valkenburg since around 1050 - and, beneath it, the Fluweelengrot, a museum marl cave linked to the ruin by centuries-old secret escape passages rediscovered in 1937.

    Look for Hilltop castle ruin & cave

    Grendelplein, Valkenburg aan de Geul, Netherlands

    Recommended by Kasteelruïne & Fluweelengrot (official), Visit Zuid-Limburg

  11. Must see · Dutch South Limburg

    Netherlands American Cemetery

    The only American military cemetery in the Netherlands: 8,000+ US war dead beneath white marble crosses at Margraten, with a visitor centre and free guided tours. Adopted graves are tended by local families to this day. Free, open daily.

    Look for WWII war cemetery

    Amerikaanse Begraafplaats 1, 6269 NA Margraten, Netherlands

    Recommended by American Battle Monuments Commission, Visit Maastricht

  12. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Dutch South Limburg

    Beluga Loves You

    Maastricht's creative-cuisine flagship in the Ceramique district, a one-Michelin-star kitchen (also rated by Gault&Millau) built on high-quality, inventive tasting menus.

    Plein 1992 nr 12, 6221 JP Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Gault&Millau Nederland

  13. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Dutch South Limburg

    Tout a Fait

    A one-Michelin-star restaurant in the old centre since 1999, chef Bart Ausems cooking a refined French-inspired menu; a long-standing fixture of Maastricht fine dining.

    Sint Bernardusstraat 12-14, 6211 HL Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Visit Maastricht

  14. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Dutch South Limburg

    Chateau Neercanne

    The only terraced castle in the Netherlands, gazing over the Jeker valley on the Belgian border, home to a Michelin-starred French kitchen (starred as far back as 1957) with baroque gardens and marl-cave cellars.

    Cannerweg 800, 6213 ND Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Relais & Châteaux

  15. Must see · Printen, Bakeries & Sweets · Dutch South Limburg

    De Bisschopsmolen

    The oldest working watermill in the Netherlands, grinding ancient Kollenberger spelt on the Jeker for the bakery next door - eat the freshest Limburgse vlaai, spelt bread and waffles right where they're made.

    Stenenbrug 3, 6211 HP Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Visit Maastricht, Stayokay City Tips

  16. Must see · Coffee & Kaffeehaus · Dutch South Limburg

    Coffeelovers Dominicanen

    Coffee on the former altar of the Dominicanen church-bookshop, poured from local roaster Blanche Dael - probably the most magical cafe in the city.

    Dominicanerkerkstraat 1, Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Grachten Beans Coffee Guide, Koffietje.nl

  17. Must see · Beer & Brewpubs · Dutch South Limburg

    Gulpener BrouwLokaal

    An eighth-generation Gulpen brewery (est. 1825) styled as the Netherlands' beer-knowledge centre - tours and a beer-sommelier tasting in the brew hall, its regional 'High Beer' pairing local beer with Limburg snacks.

    Rijksweg 16, 6271 AE Gulpen, Netherlands

    Recommended by Visit Zuid-Limburg, Gulpener Bierbrouwerij (official)

  18. Worth the detour · Dutch South Limburg

    Fort Sint Pieter

    A pentagonal 1701-02 fort on the Sint-Pietersberg guarding the Maas approach, restored and toured by guides who re-tell its sieges among casemates, loopholes and cannon, with a sweeping view over Maastricht.

    Look for 18th-century fort

    Luikerweg 80, 6212 NH Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Visit Maastricht, Explore Maastricht (Maastricht Underground)

  19. Worth the detour · Dutch South Limburg

    Kazematten (Maastricht Underground)

    A guided hour underground in the western defence tunnels dug between 1575 and 1825 - kilometres of mine galleries used to attack besiegers and, in WWII, to shelter residents from bombing. Departs from the Waldeck bastion in the city park.

    Look for Casemate tunnels

    Waldeckpark 11, 6214 BH Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Visit Maastricht, Forten.nl (Stichting Menno van Coehoorn)

  20. Worth the detour · Dutch South Limburg

    Sint-Janskerk

    The Gothic Protestant church on the Vrijthof whose bright-red, ~80 m marl tower is a symbol of Maastricht; climb it for a rooftop view across the old city.

    Look for Gothic church tower

    Vrijthof 24, Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Visit Maastricht, Wikipedia (de/en)

  21. Worth the detour · Dutch South Limburg

    Helpoort

    The oldest surviving city gate in the Netherlands (1229) and the only one left in Maastricht - twin towers of the first medieval wall, beside a preserved stretch of ramparts along the Jeker.

    Look for Medieval city gate

    Sint Bernardusstraat, Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Visit Maastricht, Wikipedia (de/en)

  22. Worth the detour · Dutch South Limburg

    Stadhuis op de Markt

    Pieter Post's Dutch-Classicist town hall (1659-64) commands the Markt, its 1684 tower ringing a 49-bell carillon over the Wednesday and Friday markets; inside are tapestries, stucco and painted ceilings.

    Look for Town hall & market

    Markt 78, Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Visit Maastricht, Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed

  23. Worth the detour · Dutch South Limburg

    Jekerkwartier

    One of Maastricht's oldest quarters, threaded by the little Jeker river that once formed the city's defence; today a village-in-the-city of makers, delis, galleries and terraces below the old ramparts.

    Jekerkwartier, Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Visit Maastricht, Wikipedia (de/en)

  24. Worth the detour · Dutch South Limburg

    Stokstraatkwartier

    A tightly restored quarter of national monuments around the Stokstraat - the city's smartest shopping lane - built over the streets of the Roman castellum.

    Look for Historic shopping quarter

    Stokstraat, Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Visit Maastricht, Wikipedia (de/en)

  25. Worth the detour · Dutch South Limburg

    Kasteel Vaalsbroek

    An estate first named in 1420 and given its stately look by Aachen cloth-baron Von Clermont, with a landscape park, ponds, a water mill, an 18th-century ice-cellar and the family mausoleum near the tri-border point; now a Bilderberg hotel whose grounds you can walk.

    Vaalsbroek 1, 6291 NH Vaals, Netherlands

  26. Worth the detour · Dutch South Limburg

    Gemeentegrot Valkenburg

    A kilometre-long marl cave toured year-round by foot or by little train past charcoal murals and sculptures - and, each winter, the largest underground Christmas market in Europe, part of Kerststad Valkenburg.

    Cauberg 4, 6301 BT Valkenburg aan de Geul, Netherlands

  27. Worth the detour · Dutch South Limburg

    Thermae 2000

    A thermal-water wellness resort of pyramided pools, saunas and a rooftop bath high on the Cauberg, fed by a natural spring drawn from deep under the Limburg hills.

    Cauberg 27, 6301 BT Valkenburg aan de Geul, Netherlands

  28. Worth the detour · Dutch South Limburg

    The rolling green heart of the Dutch 'mountains' around Epen, Gulpen and Vijlen - hollow lanes, the Geul valley and the long Vijlenerbos ridge with the country's most southern panoramas, some of the best walking in the Netherlands.

  30. Worth the detour · Dutch & Limburgs · Dutch South Limburg

  31. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Dutch South Limburg

    Les Salons (Chateau St. Gerlach)

  32. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Dutch South Limburg

    Prix de Rome

  33. Worth the detour · International & Student · Dutch South Limburg

  34. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Dutch South Limburg

    Harry's

    A buzzy, metropolitan farm-to-table brasserie in a monumental Wyck building with an open kitchen; listed in the Michelin Guide for its modern, produce-led cooking.

    Wycker Brugstraat 2, Maastricht, Netherlands

  35. Worth the detour · Printen, Bakeries & Sweets · Dutch South Limburg

  37. Worth the detour · Coffee & Kaffeehaus · Dutch South Limburg

  38. Worth the detour · Beer & Brewpubs · Dutch South Limburg

    Brand Bierbrouwerij

    The oldest brewery in the Netherlands, in the Heuvelland village of Wijlre - classic pilsner and seasonal beers from a name woven into Limburg's beer identity.

  39. Deep cut · Dutch South Limburg

    Sphinxkwartier

    The old Sphinx ceramics works reborn as a creative quarter - the landmark Eiffelgebouw, an arthouse cinema, food halls, hotels and design studios north of the centre.

  40. Deep cut · Dutch South Limburg

    Cauberg

    The Netherlands' most famous hill: a short, steep marl climb through Valkenburg that has hosted the road World Championships and is the traditional finale of the Amstel Gold Race every April.

    Look for Cycling climb

    Cauberg, Valkenburg aan de Geul, Netherlands

    Recommended by Thermae 2000 (official), Visit Zuid-Limburg

  41. Deep cut · Dutch & Limburgs · Dutch South Limburg

    Bar & Kitchen De la Bourse

    A lively brasserie on the Grote Markt long name-checked for its Maastrichts zuurvlees - a reliable central spot to try the regional stew.

    Markt 37, 6211 CK Maastricht, Netherlands

  42. Deep cut · Printen, Bakeries & Sweets · Dutch South Limburg

    Patisserie Royale

    A Maastricht institution baking artisan vlaaien since 1929; the secret of its beloved rice vlaai is a touch of almond paste. (Exact street address to confirm at geocode stage.)

    Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Time to Momo, Chapeau Magazine

  43. Deep cut · Coffee & Kaffeehaus · Dutch South Limburg

    Fixed Gear Coffee

    A specialty-coffee bar that regularly tops Maastricht's coffee rankings - a third-wave stop for a properly pulled flat white.

    Maastricht, Netherlands

    Recommended by Koffietje.nl, Grachten Beans Coffee Guide

  44. Closed — kept for the record · Dutch South Limburg

    Het Romeins Museum (Thermenmuseum) — CLOSED

    Heerlen's museum built over the excavated Roman bathhouse of Coriovallum - the oldest stone building in the Netherlands. The old Thermenmuseum closed in September 2024; a new Romeins Museum on the site is due to open in 2028.

    Look for Roman bath museum

    Coriovallumstraat 9, 6411 CA Heerlen, Netherlands

    Recommended by Het Romeins Museum (Thermenmuseum), Visit Zuid-Limburg

Ostbelgien, BE 29

Eupen · Kelmis · Hautes Fagnes

  1. Must see · Ostbelgien, BE

    Hohes Venn / Hautes Fagnes — moorland reserve & boardwalks

    Belgium's most famous nature reserve: a ~5,000-hectare high plateau of raised peat bog, heath and beech, protected since 1957 (the oldest reserve in Wallonia). Wooden caillebotis boardwalks let walkers cross the fragile Fagne Wallonne and Fagne de la Poleur without damaging the moor.

    Look for high moor nature reserve

    Hohes Venn – Hautes Fagnes, 4845 Jalhay / 4950 Waimes, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia (de/en), Visit Wallonia, Ostbelgien.eu

  2. Must see · Ostbelgien, BE

    Eupener Marktplatz & Werthplatz

    The heart of Eupen's Oberstadt: around the Marktplatz and the Werthplatz stand the tall brick-and-limestone houses the town's 18th-century cloth merchants built themselves, many with classicist gables — the architectural record of Eupen's golden age as a cloth-weaving town.

    Look for historic town squares

    Marktplatz & Werthplatz, 4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by Ostbelgien.eu, Wikivoyage (de), Eifel.de (Eifel Tourismus)

  3. Must see · Ostbelgien, BE

    Wesertalsperre (Weser dam & visitor centre)

    Belgium's most important drinking-water reservoir, holding ~25 million m³ behind a dam begun in 1936 and inaugurated in 1950; it supplies the Eupen and Herve country, the Liège suburbs and Spa. From the visitor centre you can take a guided tour that starts on the crest and descends deep inside the dam wall and waterworks.

    Look for reservoir & dam (guided tours)

    Langesthal 164, 4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia (de/en), Visit Wallonia, Ostbelgien.eu

  4. Must see · Ostbelgien, BE

    Museum Vieille Montagne (MVM), Kelmis

    Housed in the 1910 administrative building of the Vieille-Montagne zinc company, the MVM (successor of the Göhltalmuseum) tells the political, industrial and social story of Neutral-Moresnet — the tiny neutral territory that existed from 1816 to 1919 because of the calamine (zinc) ore mined at Kelmis for centuries.

    Look for industrial-history museum

    Lütticher Straße, 4720 Kelmis (La Calamine), Belgium

    Recommended by Museum Vieille Montagne (MVM), Kelmis, Wikipedia (de/en), Visit Wallonia

  5. Must see · Ostbelgien, BE

    Töpfereimuseum in der Burg Raeren

    Inside the mid-14th-century Burg Raeren, the world's only museum devoted to Raeren stoneware — over 2,000 pieces spanning 500 years of Rhenish and contemporary ceramics, including work by masters like Jan Emens Mennicken. The Raeren reference collection was awarded the European Cultural Heritage Seal in 2007.

    Look for pottery museum in a castle

    Burgstraße, 4730 Raeren, Belgium

    Recommended by Töpfereimuseum Raeren, Wikipedia (de/en), Raeren Tourismus

  6. Must see · Ostbelgien, BE

    Burg Reinhardstein (Château de Reinhardstein)

    A 14th-century rock-built fortress high above the Warche near the Robertville dam, in the Hautes Fagnes. Saved from ruin and meticulously rebuilt from 1965 using surviving documents, it is shown on guided tours through the knights' and guards' halls, chapel and living quarters, hung with armour, paintings and tapestries.

    Look for restored medieval castle

    Chemin du Cheneux 50, 4950 Ovifat (Waimes), Belgium

    Recommended by Ostbelgien.eu, Visit Wallonia, Burgenwelt.org

  7. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Ostbelgien, BE

    Restaurant Bütgenbacher Hof

    The dining room of a hotel on Bütgenbach's market square, awarded a Gault&Millau toque (13/20) and listed in the Michelin guide. Modern, well-travelled seasonal menus (a 4-course dinner and a 7-course fine-dining menu) make it the fine table of the southern lake country.

    Marktplatz 8, 4750 Bütgenbach, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&Millau Nederland, Guide Michelin Deutschland, Ostbelgien.eu

  8. Must see · Belgian & Ostbelgien · Ostbelgien, BE

    Baraque Michel

    The restaurant of the historic 1811 moor inn on the Hohes Venn, 'das Venn im Blick, das Wild auf dem Teller' as the Grenz-Echo put it — strongly seasonal regional cooking with game to the fore, part brasserie, bakery and beer hall, a classic stop on a Fagnes walk.

    Baraque Michel, 4845 Jalhay, Belgium

    Recommended by Grenz-echo, BRF (Belgischer Rundfunk), Wikipedia (de/en)

  9. Must see · Ostbelgien, BE

    Signal de Botrange

    At 694 m this is the highest point in Belgium and the roof of the Hohes Venn / Hautes Fagnes. A short flight of steps up the artificial Baltia mound (raised after WWI, named for General Herman Baltia) reaches the exact summit; beside it stand a 24 m viewing tower and a restaurant overlooking the moor.

    Look for highest point & viewing tower

    Route de Botrange 133, 4950 Waimes (Botrange), Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Wallonia, Ostbelgien.eu

  10. Must see · Ostbelgien, BE

    St.-Nikolaus-Kirche Eupen

    Eupen's landmark parish church, a twin-towered baroque hall built 1720-26 to plans by Aachen architect Laurenz Mefferdatis; the lower south tower survives from a 12th-century predecessor and the high altar (1740-44) is the work of Johann Joseph Couven. It gives the capital of the DG its skyline.

    Look for baroque parish church

    Marktplatz, 4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia (de/en), Ostbelgien.eu

  11. Must see · Ostbelgien, BE

    Stausee Bütgenbach & Sport-/Ferienpark Worriken

    A reservoir on the Warche (dammed from 1932) that became the region's watersports lake, ringed by the ADEPS Worriken sports-and-holiday park: sailing, kayaking, SUP and windsurfing, the VENNtastic Beach, a high-ropes course and lakeside hiking and biking trails.

    Look for reservoir & lakeside leisure park

    Worriken 9, 4750 Bütgenbach, Belgium

    Recommended by Ostbelgien.eu, Sport- & Freizeitzentrum Worriken (Bütgenbach)

  12. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Ostbelgien, BE

    Zur Post

    The Pankert family's hotel-restaurant in the middle of St. Vith has held a Michelin star continuously since the 1970s (his father Arno once held two). Third-generation chef Eric Pankert cooks classical French with modern accents; it also scores 15.5/20 in Gault&Millau — the blue-chip fine-dining address of the German-speaking Community.

    Hauptstraße 39, 4780 Sankt Vith, Belgium

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, BRF (Belgischer Rundfunk)

  13. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Ostbelgien, BE

    Quadras

    Ricarda Grommes opened Quadras at the roundabout on Malmedyer Straße in 2016 and won a Michelin star in 2020 (plus 15/20 Gault&Millau), making St. Vith a two-star town. Her cooking moves between French tradition and Asian precision, built on regional produce with exotic touches.

    Malmedyer Straße 53, 4780 Sankt Vith, Belgium

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Grenz-echo

  14. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Ostbelgien, BE

    Couleur Rouge

    Eupen's top-rated modern table, scoring 14/20 in Gault&Millau: French classics lifted with Asian accents, served in a warm room with a summer terrace. The Grenz-Echo's annual Gault&Millau round-up lists it among the province's best.

    4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&Millau Nederland, Grenz-echo

  15. Must see · Belgian & Ostbelgien · Ostbelgien, BE

    Arti'Choc

    A Michelin Bib Gourmand in Eupen with the feel of a cosy German Stube. Chef Daniel works fine regional produce into French staples — Zeeland mussels in creamy curry, Ondenval trout à la meunière with almonds and apples — and sells his own jam and limoncello. Good cooking, fair prices.

    Haasstraße 38, 4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Ostbelgien Direkt

  16. Must see · Belgian & Ostbelgien · Ostbelgien, BE

    Sel et Poivre

    In a restored 200-year-old farm at Eynatten, Angela and Frédéric Noël cook a seasonal French-Belgian menu that changes monthly — Bleu-Belge steak, pot-au-feu, Liège-style veal kidneys. A Michelin Bib Gourmand and a Gault&Millau address right on the German border.

    Aachener Straße 140, 4731 Raeren (Eynatten), Belgium

    Recommended by Guide Michelin Deutschland, Gault&Millau Nederland

  17. Must see · Beer & Brewpubs · Ostbelgien, BE

    Brauerei Néau

    A nano-brewery Maurice Néau built into an old workshop in central Eupen in 2018 — up to 26 different beers, from Pilsner and IPA to Belgian and experimental ales, and 'ein Eupen Pils, in Eupen gebraut' once more. Brewing courses, tastings and a beer garden open May-September; BRF has covered it as the town's craft-beer revival.

    Schulstraße 11, 4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by BRF (Belgischer Rundfunk), Ostbelgien.net

  18. Must see · Printen, Bakeries & Sweets · Ostbelgien, BE

    Kelleter Bäckerei-Konditorei

    A family Bäckerei-Konditorei run by master baker Christoph Kelleter, on the 'Made in Ostbelgien' regional-producers roster. The café (50-plus seats) serves the border region's signature Reisfladen (rice tart) alongside Belgian cream specialities like apple-cinnamon and pineapple-nougat tarts.

    Bergstraße 9, 4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by Made in Ostbelgien / Ostbelgien Info, Ostbelgien Info

  19. Must see · Printen, Bakeries & Sweets · Ostbelgien, BE

    Panciera Eiscafé

    Egidio Panciera's ice-cream café on Eupen's market square — BRF once reported it served 'the world's second-best ice cream', and on a warm day it sells up to 100 Spaghetti-Eis. House gelato and unusual sorbets (an Isabella-grape sorbet among them); the inventor of Spaghetti-Eis himself has dropped by.

    Marktplatz 3, 4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by BRF (Belgischer Rundfunk), Aachener Zeitung

  20. Worth the detour · Ostbelgien, BE

    IKOB — Museum für Zeitgenössische Kunst

    Eupen's contemporary-art museum, founded in 1993 as the International Art Centre of East Belgium. Changing exhibitions of international artists and a collection that ranges from Günther Förg to Yves Zurstrassen make it the modern-art anchor of the German-speaking Community.

    Look for contemporary-art museum

    Rotenberg 12B, 4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Wallonia, Ostbelgien.eu, Ikob — Museum für Zeitgenössische Kunst

  21. Worth the detour · Ostbelgien, BE

    Eupener Rosenmontagszug (carnival)

    The biggest carnival parade in Ostbelgien: on Rose Monday dozens of floats and foot-groups wind through Eupen's old town (in its heyday over 120), one of the two great East-Belgian carnival strongholds alongside Kelmis. A free, city-filling street spectacle each February/March.

    Look for carnival parade (Feb/Mar)

    Oberstadt / Marktplatz, 4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by BRF (Belgischer Rundfunk), Ostbelgien Direkt, Visit Wallonia

  22. Worth the detour · Ostbelgien, BE

    Naturparkzentrum Botrange (Maison du Parc)

    The visitor centre of the Hautes Fagnes-Eifel nature park at the foot of the Signal de Botrange — exhibitions on the moor's formation, ecology and history, guided walks, and the trailhead for the reserve's marked boardwalk routes.

    Look for nature-park visitor centre

    Route de Botrange 131, 4950 Waimes (Robertville), Belgium

    Recommended by Botrange, Ostbelgien.eu

  23. Worth the detour · Ostbelgien, BE

    Büchelturm St. Vith

    The 14th-century Büchelturm is the surviving landmark of St. Vith's medieval fortifications — once a town wall with seven towers and a castle, destroyed in the 17th century. Its platform gives a panorama over St. Vith and the Eifel; the key is available at the tourist information.

    Look for medieval town tower

    Büchelstraße, 4780 Sankt Vith, Belgium

    Recommended by Ostbelgien.eu, Varta-Guide

  24. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Ostbelgien, BE

    Antoine

    A well-regarded Eupen restaurant scoring 13.5-14/20 in Gault&Millau and listed in the Michelin guide — a refined, seasonal French kitchen that rounds out the capital's fine-dining bench alongside Couleur Rouge.

    4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&Millau Nederland, Guide Michelin Deutschland

  25. Worth the detour · Belgian & Ostbelgien · Ostbelgien, BE

    Reiner's Fritten & Sandwich

    A well-known Eupen friterie for the Belgian national dish done properly — double-fried frites and loaded sandwiches — ranked in the top ten of the Verviers district when the regional press ran its Fritten dossier.

    Herbesthaler Straße 299, 4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by Ostbelgien Direkt, Ostbelgien.net

  26. Worth the detour · Belgian & Ostbelgien · Ostbelgien, BE

    Alt Keris

    Brothers Roger and Alain London opened Alt Keris in 1997 in a former café building on Kelmis's main street, in the northernmost town of the DG. The Grenz-Echo's 'Mahlzeit' column praised its versatile, something-for-every-budget Belgian-French menu — frog legs and scallops to game and steaks.

    Lütticher Straße 232B, 4720 Kelmis (La Calamine), Belgium

    Recommended by Grenz-echo, Ostbelgien.net

  27. Worth the detour · Beer & Brewpubs · Ostbelgien, BE

    Ratskeller

    An atmospheric café-brasserie in the vaulted cellar beneath Eupen's historic town hall, with two terraces looking onto the church and market square. Belgian-French brasserie cooking — moules-frites and the like — served continuously from morning to late.

    Klötzerbahn 2, 4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by Ostbelgien.net, GastroGuide Euregio

  28. Deep cut · Ostbelgien, BE

    Naturzentrum Haus Ternell

    A nature-and-environment education centre of the German-speaking Community set in the Hertogenwald forest near the Weser dam, with a small fen-and-forest natural-history museum and guided hikes (in German, French and Dutch) into the northern Hohes Venn.

    Look for nature centre & forest museum

    Ternell 2-3, 4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by Ostbelgien.eu, Wikipedia (de/en), Naturpark Hohes Venn-Eifel (DE side)

  29. Closed — kept for the record · Ostbelgien, BE

    Schokoladenmuseum Chocolaterie Jacques — CLOSED

    For a quarter-century (1993-2019) Eupen's glass-domed chocolate museum let visitors watch Chocolaterie Jacques — founded 1896, based in Eupen from 1923 — make its bars beneath the roof and taste them at the end. The Eupen factory and museum closed in 2019; the Jacques brand lives on, but the visit no longer exists. Kept for the story (canon: Eupen chocolate).

    Look for chocolate museum (closed 2019)

    Industriegebiet, 4700 Eupen, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia (de/en), BRF (Belgischer Rundfunk), VRT NWS (German-language pages)

113 sights and 90 places to eat across the tri-border Euregio Maas-Rhein — anchored on Aachen (Charlemagne’s city, its UNESCO cathedral the first site ever listed in Germany) and reaching into the Eifel, across the border to Maastricht & Dutch Limburg, and into Ostbelgien. A food canon all its own: Aachener Printen and Reisfladen, Rhenish Sauerbraten and Öcher Puttes, Limburgse vlaai and zuurvlees, Belgian beer and Eupen chocolate, out to a deep Michelin bench in Aachen & Maastricht.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. The Dreiländereck canon crosses three countries: Aachener Printen and Reisfladen, Rhenish Sauerbraten (thickened with Printen) and Öcher Puttes, Dutch-Limburg vlaai and zuurvlees, Belgian beer, moules-frites and Eupen chocolate — with a deep Michelin bench in Aachen and Maastricht. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched in-language and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, UNESCO, Gault&Millau, the Aachener Zeitung/Nachrichten, WDR, Route Aachen, Eifel & Monschau tourism, Visit Maastricht, De Limburger, 1Limburg, the Grenz-Echo, BRF (Ostbelgien), DW Travel, local university & ESN guides and vetted local creators — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.
